Five files, all five declared in outputs[], nothing undeclared. Every element name is one of the six PathAssistant / three PathAssistantStep / two PathAssistantSettings elements the Metadata API field tables carry (api_meta.txt L94510-94529, L94545-94549, L124216-124224), quoted through skills/admin/path-and-guidance/references/metadata-examples.md sections 2, 3 and 5. confidence_rationale: agents/metadata-builder/AGENT.md Step 10: HIGH requires that every Questions-to-Ask row was answered from the plan rather than defaulted. Four were not. Q46 (one path per record type) and Q49 (who advances the stage) are still status 'open' in plan.json and were satisfied by assumptions A11 and A14, which the step's own inputs.defaults_applied records as defaults. Q47 (target org edition) and Q48 (auto-collapse) were never asked as step inputs at all and are carried by A12 and A13 - A13 explicitly notes Q48 carried NO proposed default and that the value true comes from the skill's metadata-examples section 3. That is the MEDIUM row, exactly: 'a documented skill default stood in for an unanswered question'. Everything on the HIGH side of the table holds - element grounding, first-pass checkers, check-outputs ok, declared outputs only - so this is not LOW. dimensions_skipped is non-empty, which the envelope schema also caps at MEDIUM.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Four of the seven admin/path-and-guidance Questions-to-Ask rows were answered by a recorded assumption rather than by a human: A11 (Q46 open), A12 (Q47 never asked on this step), A13 (Q48, which carried no proposed default), A14 (Q49 open). A fifth row - Q11's must-fill list - was answered but only partly writable: A16 records that the Decision Maker contact role cannot be a fieldNames entry, so it became guidance text. One admin/sales-process-mapping row ('walk me through the last deal you lost at proposal') has no answer anywhere on file and no documented default; it changed no element, so it did not block.

Two of the three declared checkers asserted something about these artefacts. The third, check_sales_process_mapping.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S05, printed 'Scanned 0 file(s) - nothing asserted; check --manifest-dir' and exited 0. That exit code stands for nothing: the checker lints *.yaml/*.yml/*.csv sales-process maps and a retrieved OpportunityStage value set, and this step ships none of those. amend-step cannot fix it from here (it refuses a step whose status is running), so it is left for a human before the M2 gate.

process_observations.observation: The upstream artefacts this step binds to were exact and needed no interpretation. All six picklistValueName values ('Qualify', 'Discover', 'Propose', 'Negotiate', 'Renewal Review', 'Renewal Proposed') were copied character for character out of M1-S01's two businessProcess files, including the space-not-underscore spelling of the two renewal stages, and both recordTypeName values off the recordType files' fullName. The build-scoped checker confirmed the binding: 'Checked 2 path(s): no issues found.' with zero NOTE lines, meaning it resolved both record types and matched every step name against the business processes and the value set.

The N3-F-01 warning held. skills/admin/path-and-guidance/references/metadata-examples.md section 1 still shows an Opportunity BusinessProcess whose opening value carries <default>true</default> - the shape the org rejected on 2026-09-18 with 'Cannot specify a default on: Opportunity'. This step ships no BusinessProcess, and nothing was copied from that section. M1-S01's repaired files on disk now carry no <default> at all on the opening value and <default>false</default> on the rest, which is what run 2 of the mock deploy accepted.

The checker added by amend-step on 2026-09-18 to clear a section-5 coverage WARN reads nothing in this step. check_sales_process_mapping.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S05 prints 'Scanned 0 file(s) - nothing asserted; check --manifest-dir' and exits 0. The --manifest-dir tree-walk fix of 2026-09-18 works correctly - the checker's scope is yaml/csv sales-process maps and OpportunityStage value sets, and a pathAssistants/ + settings/ tree contains neither. Run at build scope the same command prints 'No issues found.', having actually read M1-S01's OpportunityStage file. So the amendment cleared the WARN without buying an assertion, and a green tick on that acceptance-test row will mean only that a checker ran. Remedies, all a human's: re-declare the test at scope 'build' with --manifest-dir artefacts, move it to an M2 milestone test, or accept that the skill is cited for its Questions-to-Ask table (Q2 came from it) rather than for its checker - and say which, in the test's description.

Nothing in this build gives the Closed Won handoff a home, and a PathAssistant step is the cheapest one available. Q3 is answered - 'Finance needs the closed-won amount, products, discount and close date; Customer Success needs the account, products and contract start; both read the record' - and admin/sales-process-mapping's Questions-to-Ask table asks 'when a deal closes, who has to know, and what do they need from the record?' precisely because those obligations 'get built by nobody unless they are stage requirements'. This step deliberately writes no Closed Won step (the plan's own inputs.note says so, and an omitted step is the documented way to leave a chevron unconfigured), Q3 is not in this step's declared answers[], and key_fields_by_stage has no Closed Won row - so nothing was written. Worth the VP's decision at the M2 gate: one info block on Closed Won would put the Finance and CS handoff in front of the rep at the moment it matters.

The Renewal path has no page to render on anywhere in this plan. M3-S05 is the only step that writes a FlexiPage and its own note records the scope: 'Only the Enterprise page is built ... the Renewal record type falls through to the org's existing Opportunity page'. Renewal_Opportunity_Path therefore renders only if Northwind's current Opportunity record page already carries runtime_sales_pathassistant:pathAssistant, and nothing in this build asserts that it does. check_path_and_guidance.py cannot raise it either - its FlexiPage check fires only when some Opportunity FlexiPage IS in the manifest and lacks the component, so an empty tree is silent by construction. deploy-order.md section 3 carries the grep a human can run against the org.

The Renewal Proposed step's guidance names a 20% discount approval, and the provenance for the renewal ladder specifically is thinner than for the Enterprise one. Q11's answer states the gate for the Enterprise ladder ('Negotiate to Closed Won: Discount approved if above 20%'); the requirement states the rule for the team without distinguishing the two motions; and the planner put Discount__c and Approval_Status__c in key_fields_by_stage for Renewal Proposed, which is itself evidence the approval was expected to apply there. Q58's proposed default - 'one process ... used by both Enterprise and Renewal opportunities' - says the same, but Q58 is still open and is not in this step's declared answers[], so it was not treated as binding. The words are guidance, not enforcement, so nothing breaks either way; if renewals are exempt from the cap, that sentence should be struck before the M2 gate.

The step's inputs.note narrates a sibling step as blocked when the plan says otherwise: 'The Discover step's info text carries Q11's product gate in words, because M2-S04 is blocked and words are what is left.' M2-S04's status in plan.json today is 'pending', and its own note records 'Unblocked 2026-09-15: admin/validation-rules now documents the mechanism this step was waiting on'. The instruction was followed either way - the Discover step's info names the product-line gate in words - but it was written as the fallback it is no longer, so nothing here should be read as evidence that the product rule will go unenforced. Prose-level drift; amend-step --prose-only is the writer for it, and not this agent's to run.

decision_record.question: How many record types does this object have, and does each one need different guidance?
decision_record.answer: Two - Enterprise and Renewal - each with its own guidance.

decision_record.determined: Two .pathAssistant-meta.xml files; recordTypeName Enterprise and Renewal

decision_record.answer: Final as written in the requirement for both processes.

decision_record.question: Which edition is every target org, including scratch orgs?
decision_record.answer: Sales Cloud Enterprise in production, where pathAssistantEnabled already defaults true; the file ships anyway so a scratch org or Developer Edition rehearsal is not silently Path-off.
decision_record.source: assumption A12 (Q47 informational, unanswered at G1; default applied)
decision_record.determined: settings/PathAssistant.settings-meta.xml exists at all, with pathAssistantEnabled true

decision_record.question: Does anyone need to see the guidance without clicking?

decision_record.question: Who advances the stage - a person in the UI, or automation?
decision_record.skill: admin/path-and-guidance (also admin/sales-process-mapping's 'how do deals actually get closed')
decision_record.answer: The rep, in the UI; no automation writes StageName.
decision_record.source: assumption A14, the applied default for still-open Q49

decision_record.question: Which of these key fields must be filled, versus merely visible?
decision_record.answer: Q11, in full: Qualify->Discover Amount + Close Date; Discover->Propose at least one product and Next Step; Propose->Negotiate Primary Contact (Decision Maker role) and Discount; Negotiate->Closed Won discount approved if above 20%. Lead Source and Type shown for context only.

decision_record.determined: Each step's info block carries its stage's exit criteria in the requester's own terms; fieldNames carry exactly what key_fields_by_stage declares. Lead Source and Type appear in neither, because key_fields_by_stage lists them on no stage - recorded in deploy-order.md section 5 rather than silently added

decision_record.question: Which Lightning record page will render this, and what template is it built on?
decision_record.answer: Opportunity_Enterprise_Record_Page, built at M3-S05 - and only for the Enterprise record type.
decision_record.source: upstream plan (M3-S05's declared outputs and its inputs.note)

decision_record.question: Who is allowed to move a deal into Negotiation, and who actually does?
decision_record.answer: Only the owning rep, and only after the manager has seen the proposal; today reps move it whenever they like. Exit checklist: proposal sent, decision-maker identified, discount within policy or approval submitted.
decision_record.determined: The Propose step's info block, verbatim in substance - it is the one place a rep sees the rule before breaking it

decision_record.question: Do renewals run these same stages, or does the CSM run something else?
decision_record.answer: Two distinct ladders, hence two Sales Processes and two Record Types.
decision_record.source: decision D2, and M1-S01's two businessProcess artefacts read directly
decision_record.determined: Two paths with disjoint step sets; the Renewal path's two open stages are Renewal Review and Renewal Proposed

decision_record.question: Which stages does each motion actually use, and which motion is the default?
decision_record.answer: Enterprise: Qualify, Discover, Propose, Negotiate, Closed Won, Closed Lost. Renewal: Renewal Review, Renewal Proposed, Closed Won, Closed Lost.
decision_record.source: upstream artefacts - artefacts/M1-S01/objects/Opportunity/businessProcesses/*.businessProcess-meta.xml, read for the exact fullName strings

decision_record.question: Does any integration or Apex write Probability or ForecastCategoryName directly? Will any opportunity be Private, or use splits or teams?
